HMW-V13

Vendor App — Job Change Alerts

How might we ensure vendors never miss a new job assignment or cancellation when they return to the app — without push notifications?
Context: Vendor operators check the app periodically — morning, mid-day, after lunch. They do not receive push notifications in v1 (web app, no service worker yet). Their primary pain points: (1) a job was cancelled but they showed up at the pickup point anyway; (2) a new job appeared but they didn't notice it mixed into the existing list. The current table shows all jobs sorted by status/date — there is no "new since you last visited" signal. The vendor must mentally compare today's list to what they remember from last time.

Constraint: No server-side push. No email. The signal must live entirely in the web app, using localStorage to track "last seen" state.

References: VUS-040 (new job notification), VUS-041 (cancellation notification), VUS-042 (verification notification). PRD v1.2.

Option A — Inline "What's Changed" Strip Above the Table

Recommended
A dismissible strip appears at the top of the filter bar when the app detects changes since the vendor's last visit (tracked via lastSeenAt in localStorage). The strip is specific — it names the types of changes — and auto-dismisses when the vendor explicitly clears it or returns again within the same hour. No new page regions, no new nav chrome. The strip is context-sensitive: red tint for cancellations, amber for a mix of changes, gray for new-only.

What counts as "new/changed": jobs with createdAt > lastSeenAt (new) or jobs with statusChangedAt > lastSeenAt (changed). lastSeenAt is written to localStorage when the vendor successfully logs in (or visits My Jobs when already logged in, stamped at most once per 30 minutes to avoid false resets).

Pros
· Zero new structural chrome — strip sits above filter bar, dismissed by explicit action
· Context-specific tint (red for cancellations, amber for mixed) gives instant urgency signal
· "Show changes" triggers a table filter — vendor sees exactly which rows changed
· Row-level NEW/CANCELLED badges confirm which rows are affected without cross-referencing
· Auto-expires: strip gone once dismissed, or if last visit was <30min ago (same session)
Cons
· "Last seen" timestamp resets on each My Jobs visit — if vendor keeps the tab open, alert may not show
· Strip adds temporary height above the filter bar; vendors with many pills may have to scroll slightly more
· Relies on client-side localStorage — if vendor uses two devices, alerts don't sync
· "Show changes" filter must be manually cleared; no auto-reset

Option B — Nav Badge + Count Enrichment on Segment Pills

Simpler but weaker
A red dot/count badge on the "My Jobs" nav item appears whenever there are unread changes (new jobs or cancellations since last visit). The Cancelled pill gets a "NEW" sub-count to distinguish total-cancelled from newly-cancelled. No strip, no row badges. The signal is compact — vendors see something changed, but must look at the table to see what. This approach is passive — the vendor notices only if they look at the nav.

Pros
· Most compact: no extra layout regions added to My Jobs page
· Nav badge is a universal pattern — vendors recognize it immediately
· "+N new" sub-count in pills is additive info (total count stays unchanged)
· Badge clears automatically once vendor visits the page
Cons
· Nav badge tells you "something changed" but not WHAT — urgency type (cancellation vs new) is hidden
· Newly-assigned jobs not visually distinguished in the table — vendor must look for recent timestamps
· "+1 new" sub-count in Cancelled pill is easy to miss (small text inside a pill)
· Most important case (cancellation) gets weakest signal — vendor may not notice until they scroll to Cancelled tab

Option C — Dedicated "Alerts" Segment Pill

Too heavy for v1
A new "Alerts" segment pill sits between "All" and "Pending", showing a filtered view of jobs with recent changes (new or status-changed since last visit). Clicking "Alerts" filters to only those jobs. The pill has a count and auto-hides when count is zero. The filtered view uses the same table — it's just a pre-set filter combining new_jobs + recent_cancellations.

This is the most explicit model, but adds a conditional pill to the pill bar that disappears after dismissal. Vendors may find it confusing that the pill sometimes exists and sometimes doesn't.

Pros
· Most explicit model: "Alerts" pill surfaces all changes in one click
· Table is already filtered to changed jobs — no manual scanning needed
· Consistent with existing pill interaction model
· Warning icon (⚠) makes the tab immediately identifiable
Cons
· Conditional pill that appears/disappears is hard to learn (nav is not stable)
· Warning emoji is decorative — against design system (no emoji icons outside WeChat)
· 7 pills is too many for the filter bar (current is 6 — adding Alerts pushes to 7)
· "Alerts" semantically conflicts with "Cancelled" tab — vendor must understand the difference

Verdict — Option A: Inline "What's Changed" Strip

Recommended approach: Dismissible strip between the page header and filter bar. Red tint for cancellations, amber for mixed changes. "Show changes" applies a temporary filter to the table. Row-level NEW/CANCELLED inline badges confirm which rows are affected.

Why A over B: Option B's nav badge is universal but weak — it doesn't distinguish "you have a cancellation" (urgent: stop work) from "you have a new job" (actionable: assign a driver). The strip gives vendors specific, actionable information at a glance. The row-level badges (NEW, CANCELLED) close the loop: after seeing the strip, vendors can verify exactly which rows changed without relying on timestamp scanning.

Why A over C: Option C's conditional pill creates an unstable nav structure. Vendors who've dismissed alerts or have a quiet day see a different pill count. Strips are a standard pattern for transient session-specific information (similar to cookie notices, maintenance banners) that the user is expected to handle once. A pill is a persistent navigational filter.

Implementation notes:
· lastSeenAt written to vendor_last_seen_{vendorCode} localStorage key on My Jobs mount, at most once per 30 min
· "New" = job.createdAt > lastSeenAt (new assignment). "Changed" = job.statusChangedAt > lastSeenAt && job.status === 'Cancelled' (cancellation is the priority change)
· "Show changes" sets a temporary alert filter (stored in component state only, not URL). Cleared by "Dismiss" or by switching to another segment pill
· Row-level NEW/CANCELLED badges cleared once vendor clicks into the job (per-job localStorage flag)
· Threshold: alert strip appears if count > 0. Hides itself when dismissed (same session). Reappears next session if there are new changes
· If there is ONLY a cancellation (no new jobs), strip is red tint only. If ONLY new jobs (no cancellations), amber tint. If both, red tint (cancellation is higher urgency).

Open question: Should "verified since last visit" also appear in the strip? Verification (billing gate) is important to vendors — but it's less urgent than cancellations or new assignments. Suggest: verification changes listed in the strip but in muted gray text ("2 jobs verified"), not tinted. Vendor can choose to act or ignore.
